subject.title: fix(claws): harden add and remove lifecycle

question: Should the consented Claw-removal path be allowed to bypass the shared config-size-drop guard, and what focused regression proof is required to show that no ordinary agent-deletion caller receives that allowance?
rationale: The diff broadens a shared configuration-mutation capability. The PR body asserts approval, but the available context does not independently establish the intended permanent authorization contract.

options.title: Confirm narrowly and add boundary proof
options.body: Retain the bypass only for lifecycle-provenance-verified Claw removal and add focused coverage that ordinary agent deletion still rejects the guarded size drop.

options.title: Remove the bypass
options.body: Keep the existing shared guard intact and redesign Claw removal so it completes without a special config-write exception.

options.title: Pause for lifecycle-owner decision
options.body: Defer the PR until the owner of the config-mutation policy confirms whether this exception is an acceptable experimental contract.

recommendation.title: Confirm narrowly and add boundary proof
recommendation.body: Retain the bypass only for lifecycle-provenance-verified Claw removal and add focused coverage that ordinary agent deletion still rejects the guarded size drop.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the available contributor with prior merged Claws lifecycle history and can provide the concrete lifecycle rationale while a repository owner confirms the shared mutation-policy boundary.
